title.zh: 卷一百〇四 漢書6: 后妃列傳一
title.en: Volume 104 Book of Later Jin 6: Biographies 1 - Empresses and Consorts
title.raw: 卷一百〇四 漢書6: 后妃列傳一 Volume 104 Book of Later Jin 6: Biographies 1 - Empresses and Consorts

sentences.zh: 高祖皇后李氏，晉陽人也。

translations.literal: Empress Li of Gaozu was a native of Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Li, consort of Later Han Gaozu, came from Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 高祖微時，嘗牧馬於晉陽別墅，因夜入其家，劫而取之。

translations.literal: When Gaozu was still obscure, he once pastured horses at a villa outside Jinyang, and because of that entered her house by night, seized her, and took her away.
translations.idiomatic: While Liu Zhiyuan was still a nobody, he tended horses at a Jinyang country house, slipped in one night, and carried her off.

sentences.zh: 及高祖領藩鎮，累封魏國夫人。

translations.literal: When Gaozu took charge of a military province, she was repeatedly ennobled as lady of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Once he held a frontier command she rose step by step to Lady of Wei.

sentences.zh: 高祖建義於太原，欲行頒賚於軍士，以公帑不足，議率井邑，助成其事。

translations.literal: When Gaozu raised the righteous cause at Taiyuan and wished to distribute largess among the soldiers, because the public treasury was insufficient they deliberated levying the towns and villages to help accomplish the matter.
translations.idiomatic: At Taiyuan he meant to pay the troops but the state coffers ran dry, so his council weighed a levy on town and countryside to fund the bonuses.

sentences.zh: 後聞而諫曰：「自晉高祖建義，及國家興運，雖出於天意，亦土地人民福力同致耳，未能惠其眾而欲奪其財，非新天子恤隱之理也。

translations.literal: The empress heard of it and remonstrated, saying, "From the time Jin Gaozu raised the righteous cause down to our dynasty's rise to fortune, although it came from Heaven's will, it was also because the blessing-power of the land and the people arrived together; to fail to show kindness to the multitude yet wish to strip their wealth is not the way a new Son of Heaven should pity the distressed.
translations.idiomatic: She heard and objected: "Heaven raised us, but so did the people's goodwill; to squeeze their purses before you have eased their lot is no way for a new emperor to show mercy.

sentences.zh: 今後宮所積，宜悉以散之，設使不厚，人無怨言。

translations.literal: What the rear palace has stored up ought all to be scattered among them; even if the gifts are not lavish, the people will have no cause for complaint.
translations.idiomatic: Empty the palace hoards first; even thin gifts will silence grumbling.

sentences.zh: 」高祖改容曰：「敬聞命矣。

translations.literal: "Gaozu changed countenance and said, "I respectfully accept the command.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor colored and said, "Your counsel is taken.

sentences.zh: 」遂停斂貸之議。

translations.literal: "Thereupon he stopped the proposal to collect loans.
translations.idiomatic: He dropped the plan for forced loans.

sentences.zh: 後傾內府以助之，中外聞者，無不感悅。

translations.literal: Later she poured out the inner treasury to assist it; those who heard of it within and without were all moved and pleased.
translations.idiomatic: She then opened the privy purse to make up the sum, and word of it gladdened the whole court and camp.

sentences.zh: 天福十二年，冊為皇后。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Tianfu she was invested as empress.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianfu 12 she received the empress's seals.

sentences.zh: 隱帝即位，尊為皇太后。

translations.literal: When the Yin Emperor ascended the throne, she was honored as empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yin succeeded she became empress dowager.

translations.literal: Opening angle bracket marking the start of an editorial note.
translations.idiomatic: Editorial bracket opening a comment block.

sentences.zh: （案：以下疑有闕文。

translations.literal: Annotation: the text that follows is probably defective.
translations.idiomatic: Editor's note: the passage below is likely corrupt.

sentences.zh: 據《通鑒》云：隱帝與李業等謀誅楊邠等，議既定，入白太后，太后曰：「茲事何可輕發，更宜與宰相議之。

translations.literal: According to the 《Zizhi tongjian》: the Yin Emperor plotted with Li Ye and others to execute Yang Bin and the rest; when the plan was settled they entered to report to the empress dowager, and the empress dowager said, "How can such a matter be lightly set in motion? You should further discuss it with the chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The 《Zizhi tongjian》 records that Emperor Yin and Li Ye resolved to kill Yang Bin; when they told the dowager she said, "Do not rush this; take it to the chief ministers first.

sentences.zh: 」業時在旁曰：「先帝嘗言，朝廷大事不可謀及書生，懦怯誤人。

translations.literal: "Ye, who was at the side at the time, said, "The late emperor once said that great affairs of the court must not be plotted with bookish men—timidity misleads men.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ye at her elbow said, "The late emperor warned never to plot great matters with pedants—they only breed cowardice.

sentences.zh: 」太后復以為言，帝忿曰：「國家之事，非閨門所知。

translations.literal: "The empress dowager repeated her words, and the emperor angrily said, "Affairs of the state are not for the inner chambers to know.
translations.idiomatic: She pressed again; the emperor snapped, "State business is no concern of women's quarters.

sentences.zh: 」拂衣而出。

translations.literal: "He shook out his sleeves and went out.
translations.idiomatic: He flung aside his robe and left.

sentences.zh: 又云：南北軍遇於劉子陂，帝欲自出勞軍，太后曰：「郭威吾家故舊，非死亡切身，何以至此！

translations.literal: It also says: when the northern and southern armies met at Liuzipo, the emperor wished to go out himself to encourage the troops, and the empress dowager said, "Guo Wei is an old friend of our house—unless death pressed close, how could matters come to this!"
translations.idiomatic: The same work adds: at Liuzipo the young ruler meant to ride out to hearten the lines; the dowager cried, "Guo Wei is family to us—would he rebel without mortal cause!"

sentences.zh: 但按兵守城，飛詔諭之，觀其志趣，必有辭理，則君臣之禮尚全，慎勿輕出。

translations.literal: Only hold the troops and guard the city, fly an edict to instruct him, observe his intentions—surely there will be words of reason, and then the rites between lord and minister can still remain whole; be careful not to go out lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Keep the gates shut, send him a clear edict, and read his answer; lord and minister may yet mend their breach—do not rashly ride forth.

sentences.zh: 」帝不從。）〉

translations.literal: The emperor did not comply. (End of editorial note.)
translations.idiomatic: The young ruler brushed aside her warning. (End of editorial note.)

sentences.zh: 周太祖入京，凡軍國大事，皆請後發教令以行之。

translations.literal: When Zhou Taizu entered the capital, for every great affair of army and state he all asked the empress dowager to issue instructional orders to carry them out.
translations.idiomatic: After Guo Wei took the capital he still had her issue the orders that ran the realm.

sentences.zh: 是歲，議立徐州節度使赟為帝，以迎奉未至，周太祖乃率群臣拜章，請後權臨朝聽政，後於是稱誥焉。

translations.literal: That year they deliberated establishing the Xuzhou military commissioner Yun as emperor; because the welcoming escort had not yet arrived, Zhou Taizu thereupon led the host of ministers to submit a memorial and asked the empress dowager temporarily to attend court and hear government, and the empress dowager thereupon spoke in the manner of an edict.
translations.idiomatic: That year they planned to enthrone Liu Yun from Xuzhou; before the boy arrived Guo Wei had the whole bureaucracy memorialize the dowager to hold court as regent, and she assented in edict form.

sentences.zh: 及周太祖為六軍推戴，上章具述其事，且言願事後為慈母。

translations.literal: When Zhou Taizu was acclaimed by the Six Armies, he submitted a memorial setting forth the affair in detail and moreover said he wished to serve the empress dowager as a kind mother.
translations.idiomatic: When the Six Armies raised Guo Wei, his memorial laid out every step and vowed to honor her as a mother.

sentences.zh: 後下誥答曰：「侍中功烈崇高，德聲昭著，翦除禍亂，安定乾坤，謳歌有歸，歷數攸屬，所以軍民推戴，億兆同歡。

translations.literal: The empress dowager issued an answering edict saying, "The attendant-in-chief's merit and achievement are lofty, his virtuous name shines bright; he has cut away calamity and disorder and stabilized heaven and earth; songs of praise have a proper object, the celestial succession belongs where it ought—therefore army and people have pushed him forward and a hundred million share the joy.
translations.idiomatic: Her reply praised his feats, his purge of chaos, and the universal acclaim that made the mandate his.

sentences.zh: 老身未終殘年，屬茲多難，惟以衰朽，托於始終。

translations.literal: I, old woman, have not yet finished my remaining years, yet meet these many hardships; I can only, in my decay, entrust myself from beginning to end.
translations.idiomatic: I am old and worn, yet live through this storm; I can only lean on you to the end.

sentences.zh: 載省來箋，如母見待，感念深意，涕泗橫流」云。

translations.literal: Having read your letter, you treat me as a mother; I am moved by the deep meaning and tears and mucus stream across my face," and so on.
translations.idiomatic: Your words treat me as a mother might be treated—I weep as I read them.

sentences.zh: 仍出戎衣、玉帶以賜周太祖。

translations.literal: She moreover presented a campaign robe and jade belt to bestow on Zhou Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: She sent him a field robe and a jade belt as gifts.

sentences.zh: 周太祖即位，上尊號曰德聖皇太后，居於太平宮。

translations.literal: When Zhou Taizu ascended the throne, he honored her with the title Virtuous and Sagely Empress Dowager and she dwelt at the Palace of Great Peace.
translations.idiomatic: Once Guo Wei took the throne he styled her the Virtuous and Sagely Empress Dowager and housed her at Taiping Palace.

sentences.zh: 周顯德元年春薨。

translations.literal: In the spring of the first year of Xiande of Zhou she died.
translations.idiomatic: She died in the spring of Zhou Xiande 1.

translations.literal: Opening angle bracket marking the start of an editorial note.
translations.idiomatic: Editorial bracket opening a comment block.

sentences.zh: （案：隱帝未立皇后，據薛史《張彥成傳》云：隱帝娶彥成女。

translations.literal: Annotation: Emperor Yin never invested an empress; according to the 《Zhang Yancheng zhuan》 in Xue's history, Yin married Yancheng's daughter.
translations.idiomatic: Editor's note: Yin never crowned a queen; the Old History biography of Zhang Yancheng says he wed Zhang Yancheng's daughter.

sentences.zh: 《楊邠傳》云：隱帝所愛耿夫人，欲立為後，邠以為太速，夫人卒，隱帝欲以後禮葬，邠又止之。

translations.literal: The 《Yang Bin zhuan》 states: the Lady Geng whom Yin favored he wished to establish as empress, but Bin thought it too soon; when the lady died Yin wished to bury her with empress rites, and Bin again stopped him.
translations.idiomatic: The 《Yang Bin zhuan》 adds that Yin doted on Lady Geng and wanted her as empress; Yang Bin called it premature. When she died Yin demanded an empress's funeral, and Yang Bin blocked that too.

sentences.zh: 蓋隱帝在位三年，崩時年二十，故未及冊立皇后也。

translations.literal: Probably because Yin reigned only three years and was twenty sui when he perished, therefore he had not yet reached the investiture of an empress.
translations.idiomatic: He ruled barely three years and died at twenty, so he never crowned a queen.

sentences.zh: 又，《五代會要》載：漢高祖長女永寧公主，降宋延渥，天福十二年四月封，至乾祐二年十二月，追封秦國長公主。）〉

translations.literal: Moreover, the 《Wudai hui yao》 records: Han Gaozu's eldest daughter, the Princess of Yongning, was married to Song Yanwo; she was enfeoffed in the fourth month of Tianfu 12, and in the twelfth month of the second year of Qianyou was posthumously advanced to elder princess of Qin. (End of editorial note.)
translations.idiomatic: The 《Wudai hui yao》 also notes Gaozu's eldest daughter, Princess Yongning, wed Song Yanwo, was titled in Tianfu 12, and was posthumously raised to princess of Qin in Qianyou 2. (End of editorial note.)
